senses.definition: Someone who solicits customers for prostitution and acts as manager for a group of prostitutes; a pander.

quotes.text: "I'm not a whore. You're a pimp and a stupid American, and if you want to pick up a silly bitch on the street you'd better go back to the other side where you belong!"
quotes.reference: 1969, Bonnie Bremser, Troia: Mexican Memoirs, page 111:

quotes.text: A fella looking dapper / And he's sittin' with a slapper / Then I see it's a pimp / And his crack whore
quotes.reference: 2006, Lily Allen, Iyiola Babalola, Darren Lewis, Tommy McCook, “LDN”, in Alright, Still, performed by Lily Allen:

quotes.text: All my life, been hustling / And tonight is my appraisal / 'Cause I'm a hooker selling songs / And my pimp's a record label
quotes.reference: 2018, Brendon Urie, Michael Angelakos, Sam Hollander, Morgan Kibby, Jake Sinclair, Dillon Francis, “Hey Look Ma, I Made It”, in Pray for the Wicked, performed by Panic! at the Disco:

senses.definition: (African-American Vernacular, slang) A man who can easily attract women.
(intransitive) To act as a procurer of prostitutes; to pander.

examples: The smooth-talking, tall man with heavy gold bracelets claimed he could pimp anyone.

senses.definition: (transitive, African-American Vernacular, slang) To excessively customize something, especially a vehicle.
examples: You pimped out that motorcycle f'real, dawg.

senses.definition: (transitive, medicine, slang) To ask progressively harder and ultimately unanswerable questions of a resident or medical student (said of a senior member of the medical staff).

quotes.text: Only an attending physician can pimp a chief resident; the chief resident and attending can pimp a junior resident; they all three can pimp an intern.
quotes.reference: 2004, Robert A. Blume, Arthur W. Combs, The Continuing American Revolution: A Psychological Perspective, page 183:

senses.definition: (transitive, US, slang) To promote, to tout.
examples: I gotta show you this sweet website where you can pimp your blog and get more readers.

quotes.text: The trendy rehabs being pimped by the addiction industry's glossy PR.
quotes.reference: 1990 February 4, Leonard Tirado, “Privatized 'Recovery' Versus Collective Action”, in Gay Community News, volume 17, number 29, page 19:

senses.definition: (US, slang) To persuade, smooth talk or trick another into doing something for your benefit.
examples: I pimped her out of $2,000 and she paid for the entire stay at the Bahamas.

senses.definition: (Cumbria and Old Welsh) Five in Cumbrian and Welsh sheep counting.
